title: TRACE: Evaluating Execution Efficiency of LLM-Based Code Translation
abstract: arXiv:2508.11468v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have substantially improved the functional correctness of code translation, the critical dimension of execution efficiency remains overlooked. We present \textbf{\textsc{Trace}}, the first benchmark to explicitly assess efficiency in LLM-translated code. \textsc{Trace} includes 1,000 efficiency-critical tasks across C++, Java, and Python, each augmented with stress tests that reveal efficiency disparities often overlooked by small-scale tests. translated_title: TRACE：评估基于大语言模型的代码翻译的执行效率
translated_abstract: 尽管大语言模型（LLM）已显著提升了代码翻译的功能正确性，但执行效率这一关键维度仍然被忽视。我们提出了TRACE，这是首个明确评估LLM翻译代码执行效率的基准测试。TRACE包含1,000个跨C++、Java和Python三种语言的对效率敏感的任务，每个任务均配有压力测试，以揭示小规模测试往往无法发现的效率差异。利用TRACE，我们对28个具有代表性的LLM进行了广泛评估，并得出以下关键见解：1）正确性与效率常常不一致：正确性表现领先的Claude-Sonnet-4-Think仅取得中等水平的时间效率，被Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct等更小的开源LLM超越。2）低效问题既普遍存在又有规律可循：23.5%的正确翻译存在明显的低效问题，主要来源于……
tldr: TRACE是首个专门评估大语言模型代码翻译执行效率的基准，其包含1,000个跨C++、Java和Python的效率关键任务，对28个LLM的评估发现正确性与效率常常不一致，且23.5%的正确翻译存在明显低效问题。
en_tdlr: TRACE is the first benchmark explicitly assessing the execution efficiency of LLM-based code translation, featuring 1,000 efficiency-critical tasks across C++, Java, and Python; its evaluation of 28 LLMs reveals that correctness and efficiency are often misaligned, with 23.5% of correct translations suffering from notable inefficiency.
